title: Charity
tomorrow: the "blessed are" lines: whose portrait are they?

segments.voice: Yesterday, hope: an anchor that holds while the boat still rocks. The line was I hope. Today, the third of the three, the one Paul calls the greatest.

Love on an ordinary Tuesday doesn't look like a movie. It looks like a roommate who leaves the last of the coffee for you. A coworker who covers your shift without telling the whole office. A sister who listens to the same worry a third time. None of it would make a highlight reel. Paul, writing to a church in Corinth that was arguing about almost everything, gives the word for this a list. And when you look closely, every item on it is something love does.
screen: `THE LAST OF THE COFFEE.` → `NO HIGHLIGHT REEL.` → `A LIST OF THINGS LOVE DOES.`

segments.voice: Here's the start of the list, in the Douay-Rheims: "Charity is patient, is kind: charity envieth not, dealeth not perversely; is not puffed up." Charity is the older English for this love, from the Latin caritas. Today the word can sound like a donation box. Paul means something bigger and more daily. The Catechism calls charity the virtue by which we love God above all things, and our neighbor as ourselves, for the love of God. Two directions, one love. And the first letter of John won't let them come apart: "If any man say, I love God, and hateth his brother; he is a liar." That's blunt, and it's the point. In Paul's list, love isn't a mood that comes and goes. It's patient when the line is long. Kind when nobody is watching. Not keeping score. Here's one to tell a friend tonight: in Paul's Greek, love is patient isn't an adjective. It's a verb, something love keeps doing. So the question for a Tuesday isn't do I feel loving. It's what does patience, or kindness, look like with this person, today. That's why Catholics call it an act of love. Not a feeling you wait for. A thing you do.
screen: `CHARITY IS PATIENT, IS KIND.` · `GOD AND NEIGHBOR, ONE LOVE.` · `LOVE GOD, HATE YOUR BROTHER? NO.` · `LOVE IS A VERB IN PAUL'S GREEK.` · then, large: `I LOVE.`

segments.voice: Choose one person you'll see in the next day. Name what you'd like to give them, one patient or kind thing; then the thing most likely to get in the way, like being tired, or rushed, or still annoyed. Decide now what you'll do when that obstacle shows up, and rest in the plan.
Charity. Not a donation box: the love that loves God and neighbor together, patient and kind on an ordinary day.
Keep this one: I love, which in Paul's list is something you keep doing, not something you wait to feel. Until tomorrow.

chat.says: the freshman i yelled at wants training before i leave. i have zero time. do i have to?
options: Not have to. But one patient hour with her is what Paul calls charity.
No. You already gave her your cleats, so the love part is done.

chat.meaning: For Paul, love is patient and kind: things it does, not a feeling it waits for, and not a box checked once.
